record.summaryDescription:
This sticker was designed and printed while Jamie Reid was working on the Socialist magazine Suburban Press and distributed to counteract what they saw as propaganda by the government during the miners' strikes and the three day weeks of December 1973 and January 1974. The UK was being told to switch something off and conserve energy, to prove that we didn't need the miners. Reid set out to support the National Union of Mineworkers by promotion of the opposite through guerilla design. 

Jamie Reid's cut-and-paste aesthetic developed from his interest in radical politics. His artistic style developed while at art college in Croydon, where he was influenced by the ideas of the avant-garde political group, the Situationist International. The political slant to his art was aroused by the May 1968 Paris student riots, which inspired fraternal protests organised by Reid at the Croydon College of Art. These were directed with fellow student Malcolm McLaren, who would later become the manager of the Sex Pistols.
record.physicalDescription: Square black and white paper sticker with pasted-backing. Featuring an illustrated lightbulb with a grinning face, with 'Switch On Something FOR THE MINERS' in a circle around the edges.
record.materialsAndTechniques: Screen printing on paper with paste backing.

record.briefDescription: Artwork designed by Jamie Reid  for promotion and cover of the Sex Pistols's single, God Save The Queen. Black and white photographic print on black artboard.
